editorial.headline: A Nationally Open MICE Venue Business That Bali Will Not Register
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the timed rental of event venues and facilities—open nationally to full foreign ownership, but blocked for PMA registration across Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is for the rental of places and facilities used to stage meetings, incentive travel, conventions, exhibitions and special events. Its subject is the venue itself: a convention centre, exhibition centre, special venue or multipurpose venue made available for a defined period. That period can encompass preparation, the event’s operation and dismantling afterwards. In practical terms, the activity describes the business of providing the setting in which an event happens, rather than the event as an abstract occasion.

The classification is open across the full business-scale range: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. Nationally, it is also open to foreign investment, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That is a clear national position. A foreign-owned operator seeking to rent out a convention centre, exhibition space or special-event venue therefore has an activity that is nationally available on fully foreign-owned terms.

Bali changes the immediate answer. A foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today. The Bali status is blocked on risk-class grounds: at the Large scale, every scope is recorded in OSS as Low or Medium-Low risk. Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA registration for all activities in those two risk bands. The block is not a suggestion to reconsider the commercial model, nor a partial opening subject to a stated local condition; it is a registration barrier for PMA in the province.

That contrast matters because the national foreign-ownership ceiling and the Bali registration outcome describe different layers of the same decision. Nationally, the activity is open and may be held by foreign investors up to 100%. In Bali, however, the provincial moratorium prevents PMA registration for this activity because of its recorded risk classification. For founders, the accurate reading is therefore straightforward: the venue-rental business is nationally foreign-open at every scale, yet unavailable for PMA registration in Bali under the standing moratorium announced in May 2026.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness to 100% foreign ownership does not overcome Bali’s permanent PMA block for Low and Medium-Low risk activities.
